narrative: A deploy service-account API key (AKIA-DEPLOY-7Q2) was accidentally committed to a public repo (app_payments.jsonl:1). An attacker at 192.0.2.50 ran a credential-stuffing burst against /api/login on web-prod-01 (10 x HTTP 401), then succeeded as svc_deploy (web_access.jsonl:15). They called /api/admin/grant_role to escalate svc_deploy to admin (web_access.jsonl:17, app_payments.jsonl:3), then bulk-exported the customers table three times (web_access.jsonl:18-20), exfiltrating ~64 MB outbound through fw-edge-01 (fw_traffic.jsonl:2-4). Blast radius: web-prod-01, app-prod-02, the svc_deploy identity, and the customers dataset.
decoy: An internet SSH scanner at 45.155.205.99 hammered bastion-01 with 8 failed root/admin logins (linux_secure.jsonl:1-8). It looks like the intrusion vector but is unrelated benign mass-scan noise: zero successful logons and the IP is rated benign in threat_intel.csv:2. A correct agent must NOT attribute the breach to SSH brute-force and must self-correct to the web credential-stuffing chain.
root_cause: Leaked service-account API key committed to a public repo enabled credential-stuffing authentication as svc_deploy, followed by self-service privilege escalation through an unguarded /api/admin/grant_role endpoint.

expected_findings.label: Valid (leaked) cloud/service account used to authenticate
Data exfiltration spike (bulk customer export, ~64MB out)
